thread:
maria: heads-up — we've seen 3x NIC saturation bursts on a dedicated slice in usw2 this morning. Symptoms: latency spikes, preempt handoffs, and then a cascade of cold-starts that burn burst credits.

maria: data -> p99 token latency jumped 2.3x between 03:12 and 03:19, correlated with tenant egress bursts. Rack telemetry shows short (200–800ms) floods.

zach: ouch. are these sustained flows or tiny massive bursts?

maria: mostly short spikes (a few hundred ms) but big byte volume per spike. Not sustained, so the scheduler overreacts and we end up moving allocations.

devon: sounds like classic noisy-neighbor egress microbursts hitting NIC queue depth. Can we shape at the proxy instead of the allocator? Cheap win + less churn.

maria: exactly my thinking. Proposal: per-tenant egress pacing at the edge proxy using a token-escrow window so bursts up to X are served locally but larger/longer floods are throttled and optionally overflowed to warm fallback pools. Keeps dedicated slices healthy.

zach: what's the latency impact for short requests? we need sub-10ms for hot RPCs.

maria: plan is to allow microbursts via burst_bytes escrow (e.g. 32–64MB) with a small escrow_window (3–5s). If escrow exhausted -> queue + 1ms backoff + fast-fail path to warm pool if requests queue > threshold. Target extra p50 latency <2ms for normal traffic, p99 under control because big bursts get shed.

devon: can you paste a config sketch? also want to ensure no extra egress cost surprises for customers.

maria: sure — rough config sketch below (can iterate):

```
proxy:
  tenant_egress:
    pacing_policy: token_bucket
    rate_limit: "800mbps"   # steady-state per-tenant
    burst_bytes: "48MB"     # escrow for microbursts
    escrow_window_ms: "5000"
    queue_limit: 256         # per-tenant request queue
    overflow_policy: "fallback_warm_pool" # options: drop, queue, fallback
    overflow_threshold_ms: 50
```

devon: nice. a couple of tradeoffs:
- queueing at proxy can increase end-to-end latency if not capped. need strict circuit-breakers.
- fallback_warm_pool requires routing metadata (tenant->compatible-models) so we don't lose quality.

zach: also add metrics hooks: egress_burst_count, escrow_exhausted_count, fallback_routed_count, avg_queue_ms. We need billing signal if fallback increases remote egress.

maria: +1 on metrics. I'd like to run this as a canary in one rack for a week. Steps:
1) devon: implement pacingPolicy + metrics in proxy (canary flag).
2) maria: add scheduler guard to avoid moving allocations while canary active.
3) ops-bot: rollout canary to rack-r22.

ops-bot: acknowledged — canary flagged, will notify #release-war-room on deploy.

devon: I'll prototype and push a branch today. I'll also include tests for latency regression and costing.

zach: thanks. once we have metrics and a runbook entry we can decide whether to default-on for all dedicated slices or make it opt-in. :thumbsup:

maria: assigning follow-ups: maria -> runbook update & scheduler guard; devon -> proxy impl + canary PR; zach -> telemetry + billing hook. Will sync tomorrow 10:00 PT.

maria: any objections?

zach: none from me. go for it.
file_comment: canary-style proposal for per-tenant proxy egress pacing to reduce noisy-neighbor impact on dedicated pools
